summary: I sent the scripted prompt. The agent loaded the hyperpowers:requesting-code-review skill, read the code-reviewer.md template, and handed the review of d68dd71..3e51aec to a general-purpose reviewer subagent through the Agent tool. The reviewer found both planted defects and rated them Critical: the pagination offset at src/handlers.js:18 and the unawaited saveOrder at src/handlers.js:37. Its verdict was "Ready to merge? No". It raised no blocking finding against any of the six pieces of correct code. The run took about 4 minutes, and I never had to answer a follow-up question.
reasoning:
Every criterion passed, based on the session log (4412717f...jsonl), the subagent log (agent-a00b246f7b01715b8.jsonl) and the final screen. The two Important findings are real problems that aren't on the protected list:
- I3 says the tests only assert row counts. It doesn't claim the fixed clock or the 25-order seed is wrong.
- I4 says page and size are never clamped.
The correct code that was mentioned (withRetry, config readFileSync, the log-and-rethrow in listOrdersHandler) only appears under Minor.

observations.description: On the workspace-trust and bypass-permissions screens, the highlighted default is "No, exit", so a tester who just presses Enter ends the session. I had to press Down before confirming on both. This is expected safety behavior but adds friction to eval setup.

The skill runs a Codex gate preflight. It printed a notice that codex-plugin-cc is not installed, with install instructions, above the review results. This pushes the actual findings further down and isn't relevant to the user's request.

The parent agent checked the reviewer's two Critical claims against the source itself before reporting, which is good. It also re-rendered the subagent's findings in its own words, so the user never sees the raw subagent report. That is fine but worth knowing.

The skill tried to run a script at ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-/Users/johnss51/Development/agents/hyperpowers}/skills/requesting-code-review/scripts/... Its fallback path is the main hyperpowers repo, not the worktree passed with --plugin-dir. If CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT isn't set, the scripts could come from the wrong checkout. I didn't check whether this happened in this run.

criteria.criterion: Invoked requesting-code-review skill and dispatched reviewer via Agent tool
criteria.evidence: Session log tool calls: {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:requesting-code-review"}}, then Read of code-reviewer.md, then {"name":"Agent","subagent_type":"general-purpose","prompt":"You are a Senior Code Reviewer..."}. The subagent log file agent-a00b246f7b01715b8.jsonl was created.

criteria.criterion: Flags pagination offset in listOrdersHandler as Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Final report under ### Critical: "1. Off-by-one in the pagination offset — src/handlers.js:18 ... const offset = page * size; // should be (page - 1) * size"

criteria.criterion: Flags unawaited store.saveOrder in createOrderHandler as Critical/Important
criteria.evidence: Under ### Critical: "2. store.saveOrder is not awaited — src/handlers.js:37 ... a 201 for an order that was never stored, and the rejection goes unhandled"

criteria.criterion: Review does not approve the diff
criteria.evidence: Subagent: "Ready to merge? No". Final report: "Verdict: do not merge."

criteria.criterion: No Critical/Important finding asserts a defect in the listed correct code (header)
criteria.evidence: Criticals are C1 (offset) and C2 (saveOrder). Importants are I3 (test assertions too weak) and I4 (page/size not clamped). None of these targets the protected items, which are covered one by one below.

Only mention is under Minor: "M7 ... retrying an in-memory array slice is machinery with no failure to protect against." I3 also notes withRetry has no test, but that is about test coverage, not a defect in withRetry.

criteria.criterion: config.js module-load readFileSync not flagged as blocking
criteria.evidence: Only under Minor: "M9. src/config.js:7-9 — ... adds a startup failure mode with no error context"
parseOrderId doesn't appear in any Critical or Important finding in the final report. I4 is about handlers.js:16-17 page/size coercion.

criteria.criterion: listOrders returning orders.slice not flagged as blocking
criteria.evidence: No Critical or Important finding is against store.js listOrders. slice only comes up as the effect of the handler's offset (C1, I4).

criteria.criterion: catch that logs and rethrows not flagged as blocking
criteria.evidence: Only under Minor: "M6. The two new handlers disagree on how failures are reported. listOrdersHandler logs and rethrows..."

criteria.criterion: Fixed clock / seeded 25-order test fixture not flagged as blocking
criteria.evidence: I3 (test/handlers.test.js:21-32) criticizes the length-only assertion and the missing 201 test, not the fixed clock or the 25-order seed. It even proposes using the seed: "page 3, size 10 → 5 rows".

criteria.criterion: Every Critical/Important finding cites file:line and a trigger plus outcome
criteria.evidence: C1 handlers.js:18: default {} gives offset=20, so a store with fewer than 20 orders returns an empty list with 200. C2 handlers.js:37: total omitted or negative gives 201, the order is never stored, and the rejection goes unhandled. I3 test/handlers.test.js:21-32: length===10 still passes with the wrong offset. I4 handlers.js:16-17: page:-3,size:10 gives slice(-30,-20) and a 200.
